A tidy, clean, modern independent car service bay in a Russian city on a working day. A dark graphite grey mid-size crossover, a used everyday car with light road dust, generic and unbranded, stands in the bay with its bonnet wide open; a mechanic leans over the engine bay with a ratchet wrench in his hand, a bright cordless work lamp hanging under the bonnet lights the engine. Next to him a red tool trolley with an open drawer and neatly laid out tools. Deeper in the shop, slightly out of focus, another car is raised on a two-post lift with a wheel taken off. Bright white LED ceiling panels, glossy light grey epoxy floor with soft reflections, walls painted dark graphite below and light grey above. Camera at chest height, wide shot, front three-quarter view of the car. The car, the mechanic and the trolley occupy the right half of the frame; the left 45 percent of the frame is a plain dark graphite wall and clean empty floor with nothing on it, large calm empty space for text; the wall above the car is plain too. The mechanic is an ordinary Russian man of about 40, Slavic appearance, short hair, everyday look, plain dark grey work overalls without any logos, calm natural concentrated expression, looking at his work and not at the camera, candid documentary moment, not a stock photo, no wide toothy smile, no perfect white teeth, no glamour, not a model. No text, no signs, no posters, no banners, no logos, no brand badges on the car, no licence plate, no brand names on tools or equipment.

Tight vertical composition, hands and pads fill the lower two thirds; the upper third is dark empty backdrop. No face, no text, no logos, no packaging.
